## Overview

**Balor Skallfang, The Tainted**  -  tiefling barbarian of the Skallfang Clan, raised on the frozen northern frontier. Unwilling bearer of the blade containing **Khar'zul (The Flesh That Remembers)**, one of the Five Generals of the monster army. Carries a forgotten legacy and a living prison, bound to a destiny he never chose.

> *"The sword is not your burden... Your burden is choosing how to wield it."*  -  Hrothgar Skallfang

---

## Physical Description

Imposing tiefling with ashen skin crossed by faint crimson veins that glow when temper rises. Long obsidian horns (darkened after first demonic transformation). Eyes ignite with molten hues when rage takes him. Wears worn leathers and furs, carries twin handaxes at his belt. Across his back: the monstrous greatsword containing Khar'zul  -  steel turned to living flesh, veins and muscle around the guard, a single enormous yellow demonic eye peering from within.

---

## History

### Origins  -  Project Genesis
Balor is the culmination of **Project Genesis**  -  centuries of Covenant experiments breeding a mortal vessel to contain Khar'zul's essence. Only tieflings consistently survived longer than other races. The Covenant tracked bloodlines for generations until finding the perfect subject  -  a young tiefling woman. **Balor** was born from that final ritual.

### The Flight  -  Balor's Mother
Balor's mother was a victim of the Covenant, subjected to horrific experiments as part of **Project Genesis**  -  the Covenant's centuries-spanning quest to create a vessel for Khar'zul's essence. Her blood carried the exact genetic markers the Covenant had been searching for. Her full backstory is reserved for player development.

Balor was the culmination: the final product of decades of forced breeding and arcane experimentation. When he was born, his mother looked into his eyes and saw not the Covenant's weapon, but her own flesh and blood. She killed the three guards who came to collect the infant, retrieved Khar'zul's blade from the Covenant's vault, and fled into the northern wilderness. She had spent years memorizing guard rotations and mapping passages  -  she knew this facility inside out.

She survived three weeks with the infant and the blade. She discovered the blade would not leave Balor's side  -  it followed him, drawn as though it had already chosen its bearer. Exhausted and hunted, she left Balor wrapped in furs beside a trail that **Hrothgar Skallfang**  -  the clan's greatest hunter  -  was known to patrol. She tucked her family's medallion into his wrappings and disappeared into the wilderness, drawing the Covenant's hunters away.

What became of her after that remains open - she left intelligence caches across the north, but her fate is reserved for player development.

### Discovery by the Skallfang Clan
**Hrothgar Skallfang** discovered an abandoned infant beside a demonic greatsword in the frozen north. Footprints and blood trailed away. He took both child and sword. No one could lift the blade but when the infant touched it  -  a great yellow eye opened in the sword. The blade began floating, following the baby.

### The Skallfang Clan
Monster hunters of the northern frontier. Oath: *"When darkness comes... we stand. When darkness grows... we hunt. When darkness falls... we remain."* The Skallfang ancestors fought in the **First Alliance** and were entrusted with guarding the sealed blade across generations.

### Childhood and Training
Hrothgar raised Balor as his own, teaching him to hunt, fight, respect life. Balor showed remarkable physical strength from an early age. The sword's presence felt familiar. Faint whispers began, words he slowly understood.

### The Trial of the Fang
When Balor came of age at 18 (Year 498), he faced the ancient rite: alone into the frozen wilderness. When a monster threatened his hunting party, he embraced the Rage  -  but what emerged was unprecedented. His horns grew, eyes ignited, claws lengthened, crimson veins spread. Yet he never lost control. Hrothgar declared: *"It is not the darkness that defines the man... but the man who masters the darkness."* He bestowed the byname: **Balor, The Tainted**.

### The Awakening
A monstrous fiend struck the village in Year 499, hunting with intelligent purpose  -  **sent by the Crimson Covenant** to retrieve Balor and the blade. Hrothgar fell defending the lodge. Overwhelmed, Balor rushed for the greatsword. The moment he held it  -  **the world disappeared.**

### The Vision  -  Avatar of the Living Prison
Balor stood in an ashen field under a red sky before a colossal balor. The creature spoke: *"At last... You do not wield me... You carry me."* Then Balor woke  -  surrounded by the mangled bodies of the fiend and the ravaged village.

What Balor does not yet know: the vision and the blackout **happened simultaneously**. While his consciousness stood paralyzed before the balor, his body remained in the mortal world  -  but Khar'zul reached fully through the prison and **took control of his vessel**. This is the **Avatar of the Living Prison**  -  the ultimate power Project Genesis was designed to create. In this state: Khar'zul fully descends into Balor's body, Balor becomes a living vessel, the blade's power manifests without limitation, every movement controlled by Khar'zul himself. Balor's body became wreathed in crimson flame, twisting into a demonic reflection of the balor.

The **Rite of Ash** that Hrothgar taught Balor was designed to prevent this state from recurring. Every night Balor speaks the rite, reinforcing the cage. But the cage has already been opened once. It will never be as strong as before.

### The Blackout  -  What Happened
When Balor grabbed the blade, Khar'zul's essence erupted through him. His Rage became a conduit for something older and darker. In this berserker state, Balor fell upon **both** the fiend and everything around him  -  Skallfang clan members, friends he had trained beside. The blade severed the fiend's connection to its Covenant controller. The Nalfeshnee was torn apart  -  but so was much of the village. When Khar'zul's influence receded, Balor collapsed. The blade's eye remained open, its gaze carrying a knowing glint.

Balor has never received a clear answer. The surviving clan elders found him unconscious amid the aftermath. None saw what truly happened. The guilt of the unknown haunts him.

### The Last Gift of Hrothgar
Searching the ruins, Balor found a worn leather satchel containing:

**The Journal of Hrothgar Skallfang**  -  Over 200 densely written pages spanning decades:
- **On the blade's choosing:** The blade chose Balor from birth  -  the eye turned toward the infant before Hrothgar noticed the child was alive. The blade recognized a bloodline uniquely attuned to Khar'zul's essence.
- **The emergence of the eye:** ~50 years ago, Skalda Frost-Beard noted a small slit in the blade's flat. Over months it widened into the great yellow eye  -  the prison becoming a body.
- **Observing the ritual:** The Rite of Ash learned from clan elders. Chilling observation: *"The Rite does not silence Khar'zul. It only convinces him to be silent."*
- **The Covenant in the north:** Fragmentary reports of cloaked figures in the Frostmaw  -  Covenant agents watching the Skallfang territory.
- **[TODO] The Lost Century:** How the blade passed from Skallfang Clan to the Covenant  -  to be defined.
- **His mother's medallion:** Hrothgar recognized its significance  -  he found references to similar symbols in old Skallfang records of the sealing war  -  sketches of crescent-and-gem design, Infernal phrases partially translated: *"Key..." "...the Apostle's seal..." "...a name spoken in fire..."*
- **Final entry:** *"The whispers have grown louder. The eye watches Balor more intently. I fear the blade knows something I do not."*

**Crude Map**  -  Hand-drawn on cracked animal hide, marking a location deep in the northeastern mountains. Notes in elegant hand (his mother's) identify the site as an ancient dragon burial repurposed as a Covenant research outpost. Pinpoints where she left her primary intelligence cache.

**The Medallion of Vex**  -  Silver crescent-moon medallion with crimson gem. His mother's heirloom, left with him as an infant. Opens Covenant vaults keyed to high-ranking access. Contains hidden compartment accessible by pressing the crescent's tip while speaking his mother's name in Infernal.

**Wolf's-Head Carving**  -  Small obsidian wolf's head worn smooth by decades of handling. Hrothgar's personal totem. Symbol of the Skallfang hunting tradition.

**Promise-Knot**  -  Strip of dried sinew tied with three tight knots. Skallfang tradition: three knots = "I will return." Hrothgar tied it the morning of the attack, knowing the fiend was coming. Left it in the satchel for Balor  -  a final message: *I would have returned to you if I could.*

**The Recurring Name**  -  "The Crimson Covenant" written in Hrothgar's hand on scrap paper, circled and underlined so many times the ink bled through. Beneath it: *"They took the blade. They took his mother. They will not take him."*

**A Final Note**  -  Single sheet of parchment, folded and refolded:
> *"Balor  -  I have watched you grow from a child into a man stronger than I could ever be. The blade you carry is not your punishment. It is your responsibility. The answers you seek are not in this pouch  -  they are in the world beyond the Frostmaw, in the places I could not follow. Do not hate your mother. She loved you more than her own life  -  and she gave both to give you a chance. Trust the lessons I taught you more than the answers you seek.  -  Hrothgar"*

### The Exile
Realizing the Covenant would keep hunting him and endangering the clan, Balor swore at Hrothgar's grave to find the truth in Year 499. He slung the blade across his back and disappeared into the wilderness.

---

## The Blade  -  Khar'zul's Prison

A living weapon  -  steel transformed into organic matter with veins, muscles, and a single eye. Constantly whispers in Old Abyssal, offering power, testing will. The **Rite of Ash** quiets the whispers:
> *"Sleep, Khar'zul. Your prison remains. I carry your burden, but not your chains. Rest... until I call upon your strength."*

Grows in power as Balor does, unlocking new abilities and greater temptations.

---

## Personality & Traits
- **Duty-bound:** Strength exists to protect, not dominate (Skallfang creed)
- **Guilt-ridden:** Carries weight of the village's destruction
- **Determined:** Seeks truth about his origins, Khar'zul, the Covenant
- **Disciplined:** Rage is controlled  -  learned restraint alongside combat
- **Loyal:** Would sacrifice anything for family
- **Haunted:** Khar'zul's whispers test his will constantly

---

## Goals
1. Discover the truth about his birth and the Crimson Covenant
2. Keep Khar'zul contained  -  prevent him from ever being freed
3. Protect the innocent  -  live by the Skallfang oath
4. Avenge Hrothgar by stopping those who sent the fiend
